Silverleaf:

Unity's bots aren't technically "weapons", IMO. 

I disagree. They are tools being used to do battle against an enemy. That they happen to take the shape of living things (well, except for Platform Bot), isn't really relevant.

 

From Dictionary.com:

weapon

weap·on

[ wep - uh ![](upload://4U19mVsfbowr1l8rETMrSBgJTkI.png)![](upload://4U19mVsfbowr1l8rETMrSBgJTkI.png)n ]
noun
1. any instrument or device for use in attack or defense in combat, fighting, or war, as a sword, rifle, or cannon.
2. anything used against an opponent, adversary, or victim: the deadly weapon of satire.
3. Zoology . any part or organ serving for attack or defense, as claws, horns, teeth, or stings.
verb (used with object)
4. to supply or equip with a weapon or weapons: to weapon aircraft with heat-seeking missiles.
 

All of the bots (except for Swift Bot) should qualify under definitions 1 or 2. A question which might have some bearing on whether or not people agree with this is: how much autonomy do the golems have?

  • Is Unity's will required for them to act? The fact that they are destroyed when Unity is incapacitated is evidence that they might only be able to act because she controls them throughout their existences.
  • Alternatly, does she create them with behaviors that they have to follow (but her influence is not required for them to take actions once they are created)? Can they make choices on their own? Are they conscious?
These may have been answered elsewhere, but I don't recall having seen anything. I can see where, if the second scenario is the case and they have some measure of autonomy, we might hesitate to call them weapons (though I would argue that they still qualify under definition 2, above).

Thoughts?

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked: I vote "no", a bot doesn't count as a weapon.  Raptor Bot's claws and jaws are weapons, but Raptor Bot as a whole is not one, likewise Champion Bot's weapons are his fists (assuming he ever actually hits things, rather than just standing around looking inspiring), Platform Bot has pew-pew lasers, Stealth Bot has the smoke jets as "weapons" of obfuscation, etc.  The weapon has to be employed by some sort of autonomous entity, and the bots at least have the intelligence to wield them effectively, whether or not they have any actual freedom to choose when they're wielded or against what.  If you say that Raptor Bot exists only to attack things and thus is a weapon in and of himself, then you get into some ugly questions about whether a soldier in the U.S. Army now counts as a tool rather than a person as long as he obeys orders, or even metaphysical uncertainties about whether human beings ever have free will, or are simply "wielded" by their primitive kill-or-be-killed instincts.  I'd rather just draw a hard line between the actual killing implement and the being which employs it, and the bots are "beings", even if they are completely automated.  (For a realistic example that definitely doesn't involve artificial intelligence, I wouldn't characterize an aircraft carrier or even a tank as a "weapon"; they may serve as platforms for guns, but the guns could be removed and the platform would remain, able to serve other purposes or to simply exist.  Thusly, I guess you could say that my definition of a weapon is that it is irreducible to smaller unit which remains a weapon, or something vaguely along those lines.)
